To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel TALE target prediction approach, that we demonstrate that this approach is more accurate than previous approaches, that we propose to replace promoter scans by genome scans, that we demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, and that we identify novel targets.
we propose a novel TALE target prediction model that makes use of quantitative data and that this model allows us to predict novel TALE targets, some of which may be of regulatory nature.

a) a novel approach for the prediction of target genes for pathogen-derived transcription activator-like effector proteins yields higher prediction accuracy and, hence, allows for a more reliable identification of potential targets and b) the search for targets of such proteins should not be restricted to promoters of annotated protein-coding genes, but may be extended to a genome-wide search.
In summary, our research is concerned with
novel approaches and strategies for target prediction of TALEs.

novel computational approaches for TALE target identification and the discovery of novel targets that may contribute to a better understanding of Xanthomonas infections and may help to develop novel disease management strategies.
improving the understanding of TALEs and, thereby, of plant-pathogenic X. oryzae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the novel PrediTALE approach is more accurate in predicting TALE targets, and the genome-wide search strategy may yield additional targets that may be of regulatory function.
our approach allows for a more accurate prediction of target genes and, by this, for more detailed understanding of Xanthomonas virulence mechanisms.
our approach is able to identify novel putative TALE target genes that were previously not considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our novel model learned from experimental data allows us to predict new targets for TALEs and, hence, to gain novel insight into the infection strategy of plant-pathogenic Xylella and Xanthomonas.
TALE target prediction is now more accurate than before and that we are able to detect more targets.

we present a new tool to identify potential targets for a given TALE, which may help to better understand the biology of Xanthomonas infections and, eventually, to develop novel strategies to protect plants against these diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TALE target prediction is not a solved problem yet and that new strategies may yield novel insights into the infection strategies of Xanthomonas.
the combination of a computational prediction approach and a genome-wide search for target boxes may help us to understand the role of TALEs for plant-pathogen interactions.
TALE target prediction may be improved by a combination of novel insights and a broad data basis.
